questions.q: What is Japan’s national flower?
questions.fact: Cherry blossoms symbolize the fleeting beauty of life.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain in Japan?
questions.fact: Mount Fuji rises 3,776 meters above sea level.

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.fact: The capital was moved to Tokyo in 1869.

questions.q: What is Japan’s main currency?
questions.fact: The yen was introduced in 1871.

questions.q: What is a traditional Japanese inn with tatami floors called?
questions.fact: Guests at ryokan sleep on futons laid on tatami mats.

questions.q: Which ocean lies to the east of Japan?
questions.fact: Japan is surrounded by the Pacific Ocean.

questions.q: What is the Japanese tradition of viewing cherry blossoms called?
questions.fact: Hanami means enjoying picnics under blooming sakura trees.

questions.q: What is the main Shinto religious complex called?
questions.fact: Shinto places of worship are known as shrines.

questions.q: Which dish is most closely associated with Japan?
questions.fact: Sushi is one of Japan’s most iconic dishes.

questions.q: Who is Japan’s head of state according to the Constitution?
questions.fact: The Emperor is the symbol of the nation; political power rests with the parliament.

questions.q: What is Japan’s national sport?
questions.fact: Sumo wrestling dates back over 1,500 years and is deeply tied to Shinto rituals.

questions.q: Which Japanese city was the first to suffer an atomic bombing?
questions.fact: Hiroshima was bombed on August 6, 1945, leading to Japan’s surrender in WWII.

questions.q: What is the name of the Japanese bullet train?
questions.fact: The Shinkansen can reach speeds of over 300 km/h.

questions.q: Which Japanese company created the PlayStation?
questions.fact: Sony released the first PlayStation console in 1994.

questions.q: What is Japan’s main religion alongside Shinto?
questions.fact: Most Japanese people practice both Shinto and Buddhism in daily life.

questions.q: What is the traditional Japanese garment called?
questions.fact: Kimono literally means 'thing to wear'.

questions.q: Which Japanese dish consists of noodles served in a hot broth?
questions.fact: Ramen has Chinese origins but became a Japanese national favorite.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for a festival?
questions.fact: There are over 200,000 matsuri celebrated across Japan each year.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is famous for deer roaming freely in its parks?
questions.fact: In Nara, deer are considered sacred messengers of the gods.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for 'thank you'?
questions.fact: ‘Arigatou’ is one of the most commonly used words in Japan.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for 'cartoon' or 'comic'?
questions.fact: Manga is a multi-billion dollar industry with global influence.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for animated films or series?
questions.fact: Anime literally means 'animation' in Japanese but usually refers to Japanese-style animation.

questions.q: Which Japanese animation studio created 'Spirited Away'?
questions.fact: ‘Spirited Away’ won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2003.

questions.q: Who is the creator of the Pokémon franchise?
questions.fact: Tajiri was inspired by his childhood love of collecting insects.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for 'goodbye'?
questions.fact: ‘Sayonara’ literally means ‘if it must be so’ — used when parting for a long time.

questions.q: Which city was Japan’s capital before Tokyo?
questions.fact: Kyoto was Japan’s capital for over a thousand years.

questions.q: What do Japanese people traditionally remove before entering a home?
questions.fact: Removing shoes keeps the tatami mats and floors clean.

questions.q: Which Japanese car company produces the Corolla?
questions.fact: The Toyota Corolla is one of the best-selling cars of all time.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of paper folding called?
questions.fact: Origami is often used to symbolize peace and mindfulness.

questions.q: What is the name of Japan’s parliament?

answers.text: The House of the Rising Sun

questions.fact: Japan’s National Diet consists of two houses: the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of flower arrangement called?
questions.fact: Ikebana emphasizes balance, harmony, and simplicity in floral design.

questions.q: Which Japanese city hosts the famous Fushimi Inari Shrine with thousands of red gates?
questions.fact: The shrine features over 10,000 vermilion torii gates dedicated to the god of prosperity.

questions.q: What are Japan’s traditional wooden sandals called?
questions.fact: Geta are worn with yukata or kimono and help keep the fabric from touching the ground.

questions.q: Which Japanese martial art focuses on using a sword?
questions.fact: Kendo means 'the way of the sword' and uses bamboo swords called shinai.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for 'cute'?
questions.fact: The concept of 'kawaii' shapes much of Japan’s pop culture, from fashion to mascots.

questions.q: Which Japanese island is the largest by area?
questions.fact: Honshu is home to Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka — Japan’s main economic and cultural centers.

questions.q: What is the Japanese practice of repairing pottery with gold called?
questions.fact: Kintsugi turns broken ceramics into unique works of art, symbolizing beauty in imperfection.

questions.q: Which famous Japanese company’s mascot is Pikachu?
questions.fact: Nintendo launched Pokémon in 1996; Pikachu became its global ambassador.

questions.q: Which Japanese artist became famous for the painting 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa'?
questions.fact: Hokusai’s print is one of the most recognized artworks in the world.

questions.q: What are Japanese comics for adults called?
questions.fact: Seinen manga target adult men, featuring complex plots and mature themes.

questions.q: Which mountain is Japan’s highest peak?
questions.fact: Mount Fuji rises 3,776 meters high and is a sacred symbol of Japan.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for traditional performing arts combining dance and drama?
questions.fact: Kabuki features colorful makeup, bold acting, and elaborate costumes.

questions.q: Which Japanese food consists of raw fish served over rice?
questions.fact: Sushi has become a global delicacy but originated as street food.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for hospitality and mindful service?
questions.fact: Omotenashi is the spirit of anticipating guests’ needs without being asked.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is famous for its Peace Memorial Park?
questions.fact: Hiroshima’s Peace Park honors victims of the atomic bombing and promotes peace.

questions.q: What is Japan’s traditional tea ceremony called?
questions.fact: The tea ceremony blends art, philosophy, and mindfulness in every gesture.

questions.q: Which animal is considered sacred in Nara Park?
questions.fact: Nara’s deer are believed to be messengers of the Shinto gods.

questions.q: Which Japanese car brand created the luxury line ‘Lexus’?
questions.fact: Toyota launched Lexus in 1989 to compete in the premium car market.

questions.q: What is the traditional Japanese short poem with 17 syllables called?
questions.fact: Haiku captures the beauty of fleeting moments, often inspired by nature.

questions.q: Which Japanese festival celebrates cherry blossoms?
questions.fact: During Hanami, people gather under blooming sakura trees to enjoy picnics and celebrate spring.

questions.q: What is the name of Japan’s famous high-speed train?
questions.fact: The Shinkansen, or 'bullet train', reaches speeds of up to 320 km/h.

questions.q: Which Japanese city hosted the 2020 Summer Olympics?
questions.fact: Due to the pandemic, the Tokyo 2020 Olympics were actually held in 2021.

questions.q: What is the traditional Japanese robe called?
questions.fact: The kimono is often worn on special occasions like weddings or festivals.

questions.q: What do Japanese students commonly wear to school?
questions.fact: Japanese school uniforms were inspired by European naval outfits.

questions.q: Which Japanese company created the PlayStation console?
questions.fact: The original PlayStation was released in 1994 and revolutionized gaming worldwide.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for a person obsessed with anime or games?
questions.fact: ‘Otaku’ used to have a negative connotation, but now it’s proudly used by fans.

questions.q: Which Japanese art uses miniature trees?
questions.fact: Bonsai is the art of cultivating small trees that mimic the shape of full-sized ones.

questions.q: Which Japanese electronic company invented the Walkman?
questions.fact: The Sony Walkman changed how the world listens to music on the go.

questions.q: What is the name of Japan’s largest fish market, located in Tokyo?
questions.fact: Tsukiji Market was once the world’s largest seafood market, famous for tuna auctions.

questions.q: What do Japanese people traditionally eat on New Year’s Day?
questions.fact: Osechi Ryori is a colorful meal packed into lacquered boxes, symbolizing happiness and luck for the year ahead.

questions.q: Which Japanese dish is made by grilling chicken skewers over charcoal?
questions.fact: Yakitori literally means 'grilled bird' and is a common snack at izakaya pubs.

questions.q: What does the word 'samurai' literally mean?
questions.fact: Samurai means 'to serve' and refers to Japan’s warrior class loyal to their lords.

questions.q: What is Japan’s most famous theme park inspired by anime and Studio Ghibli films?
questions.fact: Ghibli Park opened in 2022 and lets visitors step into scenes from classic films like ‘Totoro’ and ‘Spirited Away’.

questions.q: What is Japan’s national sport?
questions.fact: Sumo dates back over 1,500 years and includes rituals tied to Shinto traditions.

questions.q: Which Japanese flower is the national symbol of the country?
questions.fact: Cherry blossoms, or sakura, symbolize the beauty and impermanence of life.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is home to the Golden Pavilion (Kinkaku-ji)?
questions.fact: Kinkaku-ji is covered in gold leaf and reflects beautifully in the surrounding pond.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for 'cartoon' or 'animated film'?
questions.fact: Anime has become a global phenomenon influencing art and storytelling worldwide.

questions.q: What is the name of the Japanese art of folding paper?
questions.fact: Origami teaches patience and precision — a simple sheet of paper can become a crane or dragon.

questions.q: Which Japanese company is known for creating Mario and Zelda?
questions.fact: Nintendo’s characters, created by Shigeru Miyamoto, defined generations of gaming.

questions.q: What is Japan’s currency called?
questions.fact: The yen (¥) has been Japan’s currency since 1871.

questions.q: What is the name of Japan’s traditional flower arranging art?
questions.fact: Ikebana focuses on harmony, balance, and simplicity — every stem and leaf has meaning.

questions.q: Which Japanese term describes the aesthetic of finding beauty in imperfection?
questions.fact: Wabi-sabi celebrates the imperfect, impermanent, and incomplete — a core concept in Japanese art.

questions.q: What is Japan’s most famous castle, located in Himeji?
questions.fact: Himeji Castle, known as the 'White Heron', is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for the 'way of the warrior'?
questions.fact: Bushido emphasizes honor, courage, and loyalty — the moral code of the samurai.

questions.q: What is Japan’s national holiday celebrating the Emperor’s birthday called?
questions.fact: Tennō Tanjōbi changes date depending on the reigning Emperor — currently celebrated in February.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is famous for its futuristic architecture and neon nightlife?
questions.fact: Tokyo blends tradition and technology — ancient temples stand beside LED skyscrapers.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for traditional wooden clogs or sandals?
questions.fact: Geta elevate the foot off the ground to protect kimonos from mud and rain.

questions.q: Which sea creature is often associated with Japan’s cuisine and symbolism of intelligence?
questions.fact: Octopus, or 'tako', appears in street snacks like takoyaki and symbolizes adaptability.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold called?
questions.fact: Kintsugi means 'golden joinery' — embracing flaws as part of an object’s history.

questions.q: Which city was Japan’s first capital before Kyoto?
questions.fact: Nara was Japan’s first permanent capital, built in 710, home to the Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji.

questions.q: Which Japanese island is known for its active volcano, Mount Sakurajima?
questions.fact: Mount Sakurajima is one of the world’s most active volcanoes and regularly releases ash over Kagoshima City.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for a traditional short poem of 17 syllables?
questions.fact: Haiku often captures a fleeting moment of nature and emotion in just 17 syllables.

questions.q: Which Japanese company invented instant noodles?
questions.fact: Momofuku Ando of Nissin Foods created instant noodles in 1958 to fight food shortages after WWII.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for a traditional sliding paper door?
questions.fact: Shoji screens are made from translucent paper and wooden frames to let natural light pass softly into rooms.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is known for its Peace Memorial Park and Atomic Bomb Dome?
questions.fact: Hiroshima Peace Park commemorates the victims of the 1945 atomic bomb and promotes global peace.

questions.q: What is the Japanese practice of drinking tea as a meditative ceremony called?
questions.fact: Chadō combines art, philosophy and mindfulness, emphasizing grace and respect in every movement.

questions.q: Which Japanese mountain range is called the 'Japanese Alps'?
questions.fact: The Hida Mountains in central Honshu are nicknamed the Japanese Alps for their snow-covered peaks and alpine villages.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for a portable lunch box with compartments?
questions.fact: A bento is a balanced meal in a box — often beautifully arranged with rice, fish, vegetables and fruit.

questions.q: Which famous Japanese animation director created 'Spirited Away'?
questions.fact: Miyazaki’s ‘Spirited Away’ won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003 and is beloved worldwide.

questions.q: Which Japanese city is considered the birthplace of sushi?
questions.fact: Tokyo was once called Edo, where ‘Edo-style’ sushi was created — fresh fish pressed onto vinegared rice for quick street meals.

questions.q: What is the Japanese name for the famous 'floating' torii gate in Miyajima?
questions.fact: The red torii gate of Itsukushima appears to float on the sea at high tide — one of Japan’s most iconic views.

questions.q: What is the traditional Japanese garment worn on special occasions?
questions.fact: The kimono, meaning ‘thing to wear’, is tied with an obi belt and symbolizes grace and respect.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of ink painting called?
questions.fact: Sumi-e uses simple black ink strokes to express emotion and nature’s essence — ‘less is more’ in Japanese art.

questions.q: What is the name of Japan’s famous high-speed train network?
questions.fact: The Shinkansen has been running since 1964 and reaches speeds over 320 km/h — with legendary punctuality.

questions.q: Which Japanese festival celebrates the blooming of cherry blossoms?
questions.fact: Hanami means ‘flower viewing’ — people gather under sakura trees to picnic, sing, and celebrate spring.

questions.q: Which Japanese car brand’s logo features three diamonds?
questions.fact: The name ‘Mitsubishi’ means ‘three diamonds’, symbolizing reliability and integrity.

questions.q: Which Japanese city hosts one of the world’s largest fish markets?
questions.fact: Tokyo’s Toyosu Market replaced the famous Tsukiji Market — famous for tuna auctions and sushi stalls.

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for a hot spring bath?
questions.fact: Onsen are natural volcanic hot springs — visiting them is a cherished relaxation ritual in Japan.

questions.q: Which Japanese city was historically the seat of the shogunate?
questions.fact: Edo, now Tokyo, was the political center during the Tokugawa Shogunate (1603–1868).

questions.q: What is the Japanese term for the 'divine wind' that protected Japan from Mongol invasions?
questions.fact: Kamikaze — ‘divine wind’ — refers to typhoons that destroyed invading Mongol fleets in the 13th century.
